name: The Hay Adams
positioning: The Hay-Adams, a hotel built as a residential hotel in the 1920s, overlooking the White House and Lafayette Square in Washington, DC
best_for: Travelers who want views of the White House and Lafayette Square
Guests who like historic interiors, a historic bar and a fine-dining restaurant on site

facts.text: The Hay-Adams was originally designed and built as a residential hotel in the 1920s.
The hotel looks out over the White House, Lafayette Square and St. John's Church.
The hotel's address is 800 16th St. NW, Washington, D.C.
The interiors combine Corinthian, Doric and Ionic columns, walnut wainscoting, and ceilings with Elizabethan, Italian and Tudor motifs.
The Lafayette is the hotel's fine-dining restaurant, serving upscale contemporary American cuisine.
The Lafayette is filled with natural light by day and candlelight in the evening.
The Lafayette's Private Dining Room has an ornamental fireplace and views of Lafayette Park.
Off The Record is a historic bar in the hotel's basement.
Top of the Hay, the hotel's event space, has a wraparound balcony and French doors.
The hotel runs an Author Series.
The Hay-Adams was awarded Two MICHELIN Keys in the MICHELIN Guide Hotel Selection 2026.

highlights.text: The Federal Suite, the Presidential Suite and the White House View Junior Suites have private balconies with views of the White House.
Off The Record, the hotel's bar, displays a collection of artwork created by editorial cartoonists.
Top of the Hay is an event space with views over the White House and the city skyline.
Each quarter, Off The Record partners with another hotel on a cocktail that brings the spirit of that hotel's destination to Washington, DC.

considerations.text: The fitness center is small, and there is no on-site pool or spa.
Rooms do not have in-room coffee and tea facilities.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the hotel's luxury positioning.
